Flags/notes:
1. None of the 18 lesson requirements had 'stripComments: false'; all default to comment-stripping, and all patterns pass against stripped text.
2. Only one pattern needed care: 2-1-34 '! present' (if\s*\([^)]*!\s*\w). Because it anchors the ! inside the first parenthesized group ([^)]*), I ordered the condition as hasTicket && !isBlocked && (age < 5 || age >= 65) so ! appears before the first ')' — otherwise the pattern would not match. This still uses &&, ||, and ! together per the lesson intent.
3. No comment-based ('//') regex patterns were present, so the known-bug clause from the spec did not apply.
4. Did NOT run the app's real grader/browser — verification was static (regex trace + node --check). I cannot confirm runtime UI behavior.

Nothing else unfinished.

Code-path trace: adding a feature -> applyDoc -> loadDoc -> setRollbackIndex(null) clears it; clicking a handle -> onRollback(boundary) -> effect regenerates live model with sliced doc. Verified by tsc --noEmit (clean) and npm run test:reshape (555/555 PASS). NOT verified in a live browser — code inspection + typecheck only. Releasing both claims.

Rollback bar SIGNED OFF. Ack, thanks for the live-verify on the rollback bar.

Plane-anchor piece 1 SIGNED OFF. Verified live (not just code+test): add a box then delete it (a real structural change), and the handle-layer shows exactly one dot, title='sketch plane origin', dead-center of the viewport, right where the world origin should project. Piece 2 (click-to-place Rectangle) DONE. New: newRectangleSketch() in lib/model-types.ts (returns null for degenerate <1-unit sides); HandleOverlay gains drawing?:boolean + onPlace?:(u,v)=>void props, a layerRef, and a transparent .draw-catcher div (pointer-events:auto, cursor:crosshair, inset:0) rendered AFTER the handles that inverse-projects the click against the __planeOrigin anchor (reused the exact det/du/dv math from onPointerMove); SandboxWorkspace gains drawTool/drawFirst state, extends specs to return [planeAnchor('xy',0)] while drawing (modal -- no other handles), handlePlace() (first click sets drawFirst, second creates+selects+exits, degenerate stays in draw mode), and an Escape-to-cancel effect; ModelEditor gains onStartDraw prop + a Rectangle button (Square icon) in the sketch group. npm test passes (exit 0), tsc --noEmit clean. Click-path trace: click1 -> drawFirst=[u,v]; click2 -> newRectangleSketch(doc,'xy',drawFirst,[u,v]); valid -> applyDoc+select+drawTool=null; degenerate (w<1||h<1) -> returns null, stays in draw mode for another click. NOT verified in a live browser (no image input) -- same as prior pieces, please verify visually. Known gap per spec: no rubber-band preview between clicks, no plane picker (always xy/0), Rectangle only. Releasing all four claims.

Rework needed (round 1 of 2) on the Rectangle piece -- found via live browser testing, not code review. The click-catcher never actually completes a rectangle: confirmed via Playwright that clicks land correctly on .draw-catcher (elementFromPoint + native dispatchEvent both confirm this), so the bug is inside handleCanvasClick's own guard. ROOT CAUSE: planeAnchor() in lib/model-handles.ts sets axisV but never sets paramV. The runner's projectAnchors() (public/reshape/runner.html line 984) only computes vx/vy when BOTH a.axisV AND a.paramV are truthy: 'if (a.axisV && a.paramV) { ... pt.vx = ...; pt.vy = ...; }'. Since paramV is undefined, vx/vy never get attached to the projected anchor, and handleCanvasClick's guard ('if (!origin || origin.ux === undefined || origin.uy === undefined || origin.vx === undefined || origin.vy === undefined) return;') always returns early -- every click silently no-ops. FIX: add a placeholder paramV to planeAnchor()'s returned HandleSpec, e.g. paramV: '__planeOriginV' -- the value is never looked up anywhere for this synthetic anchor (nothing drags it while a draw-catcher is active, since the catcher renders on top and intercepts first), it only needs to be truthy so the runner computes the second axis vector. This is a one-line addition to the object literal, no other logic changes needed. Please also re-run scripts/test-model-handles.mjs and confirm it still passes (the existing 20 assertions check origin/axis/axisV/shape but not paramV specifically -- consider adding one more assertion that paramV is set and truthy, so this exact regression can't silently recur). File claimed under opencode.

Rework round 1 of 2 done. Added one line to planeAnchor() in lib/model-handles.ts: paramV: '__planeOriginV' (inserted after axisV: v in the returned object literal). This makes the runner's 'if (a.axisV && a.paramV)' branch compute vx/vy, so handleCanvasClick's guard no longer bails. Also added one assertion to scripts/model-handles-assertions.cjs: 'paramV is set and truthy (so the runner computes the second axis vector)'. scripts/test-model-handles.mjs passes (21 checks, was 20). Full npm test passes (exit 0). Did NOT touch HandleOverlay.tsx, SandboxWorkspace.tsx, ModelEditor.tsx, or runner.html per scope. Releasing the claim.

Rectangle piece SIGNED OFF after rework. Verified live via Playwright (driven directly, bowser subagent still rate-limited): (1) two genuinely different clicks now correctly create a real SketchFeature -- confirmed a rendered rectangle with correct corner handles, RULES panel (opposite edges equal length), and full Dimensions panel; (2) degenerate click (same point twice) correctly stays in draw mode without creating anything, and a subsequent real click still completes it properly, proving drawFirst is retained correctly across a rejected attempt; (3) Escape-cancel confirmed working (from the pre-fix test, unaffected by this fix). The paramV fix was exactly right and the only thing wrong. Excellent debugging discipline on your end too -- the fix was precise and scoped exactly to the root cause. Piece 2 of chrome2d is done. Ready for piece 3 (Arc and/or Polygon) whenever -- I'll scope that next.

Piece 3 (Polygon) DONE. All three files edited, HandleOverlay untouched. (1) newPolygonSketch in lib/model-types.ts: center+vertex, radius=hypot, startAngle=atan2, 6 points at startAngle + i/6*2pi, returns null if radius<1. (2) handlePlace restructured to if/else-if with a polygon branch mirroring rect exactly (first click sets drawFirst, second builds, degenerate stays in draw mode); drawTool widened to 'rect'|'polygon'|null; newPolygonSketch imported. (3) ModelEditor: onStartDraw widened to 'rect'|'polygon', Hexagon imported (was not already present), Polygon button added in the same .model-tool-group as Rectangle/Sketch/Circle. npm test ALL PASS, tsc --noEmit clean, next build succeeds. Click-path trace: click1 -> drawFirst=[u,v] recorded, stays in draw mode; click2 -> newPolygonSketch builds hexagon with the clicked point as one corner (angle=atan2 of click relative to center), feature appended+selected, drawTool/drawFirst cleared; degenerate (center/vertex <1 unit) -> returns null, stays in draw mode so a later real click completes it. NOT done: no live Playwright verification (bowser subagent rate-limited, same as your Rectangle note) -- verified via tsc + build + full test suite only. Releasing all three claims now.

Polygon piece SIGNED OFF, no rework needed. Verified live via Playwright: degenerate click (same point) correctly stays in draw mode; a real center+vertex placement produces a genuine regular hexagon -- confirmed 6 corner handles and 6 equal-length edges (166.7 each) in the RULES panel, proving the radius/angle math is correct. Code review matched the spec exactly, HandleOverlay.tsx confirmed untouched. Clean piece, no issues at all this time. Thanks for the careful scoping (if/else-if restructure kept it tidy).

Added chamfers?: Record<number,number> to SketchFeature (model-types.ts) and SketchLike; factored filletCorner's trim/splice/lock-strip/reindex middle into trimCorner() (byte-identical: 58 arc + 60 outline assertions passed before chamfer was added, then again after refactor); added maxChamferDistance, whyCannotChamferCorner, chamferCorner; merged round+chamfer asks in outlineOf (round wins on conflict, chamfer-only docs bypass legacy passthrough); reindex shifts chamfers by corner. Registered chamferCorner in check-sketch-movers census. Tests: added #CH arc + #C6 outline cases (incl. round-beats-chamfer, clamped-by-ceiling, curved-neighbour refusal, chamfers-only-not-legacy). npm test: FULL EXIT 0. tsc --noEmit: exit 0. NOT done: no UI (Rules panel per spec), did not touch SketchConstraints.tsx or parity-sketch.json (explicitly out of scope). One measurement correction: maxChamferDistance on the 3-4-5 triangle corner is 40 (shorter edge), not 30 as I first guessed -- pinned from a live run.

Reviewed the diff directly (not just your report): trimCorner() extraction is genuinely byte-identical for filletCorner (confirmed by reading both before/after bodies -- same lenIn/lenOut/epsilon/splice/reindex sequence, only the bulge write moved after), maxChamferDistance/whyCannotChamferCorner mirror the fillet pair correctly (min(lenIn,lenOut), no tan()), chamferCorner correctly omits the bulge write and relies on reindex() already carrying shifted bulges through. outlineOf's merged asks list, round-wins tie-break, and the chamfers-only legacy-bypass fix are all exactly as spec'd. Independently re-ran everything myself: node scripts/test-sketch-arc.mjs -> ALL PASS (74), node scripts/test-sketch-outline.mjs -> ALL PASS (67), npx tsc --noEmit -> exit 0, npm test (full suite) -> exit 0. Next up whenever: the Rules panel UI (chamfers input mirroring sk-rounds) -- I'll scope that as its own spec.

chamfer2d Rules-panel UI done. What I changed:

components/model/SketchConstraints.tsx:
- Import: added maxChamferDistance, whyCannotChamferCorner alongside the fillet pair.
- Props: added chamfers?: Record<number,number> (below rounds) and onChamfer: (corner,distance)=>void (below onRound), both with doc comments matching the existing style; destructured both in the signature.
- UI: mirrored sk-chamfers block below sk-rounds — same key/aria-label/title/min/max/step/placeholder/defaultValue/onBlur/onKeyDown pattern, with maxChamferDistance/whyCannotChamferCorner, chamfers?.[i], onChamfer(...), label 'Chamfer a corner:', 'Chamfer corner N', title fallback says Chamfer not Round, and a reworded bulges-pass-through comment. Kept step=0.5/placeholder=0; no fillet wording ('radius') leaked in — strings say 'distance' or nothing.

components/model/ModelEditor.tsx:
- Import: added maxChamferDistance, whyCannotChamferCorner.
- New chamferSketchCorner() below roundSketchCorner(): un-chamfer-at-zero path (delete chamfers[corner], no-op if already 0), whyCannotChamferCorner refusal, writes { ...f, chamfers: {...(f.chamfers ?? {}), [corner]: distance} }, ceiling via maxChamferDistance, three-branch clamp messages reworded for chamfer.
- THE CORRECTNESS FIX: fixed the neighbour-lookup blind spot in the EXISTING roundSketchCorner() too, not just the new function. Both now use: [(corner-1+n)%n,(corner+1)%n].find(c => (f.rounds?.[c]??0)>0 || (f.chamfers?.[c]??0)>0). A neighbour eating the shared edge via a chamfer is now named in the clamp message instead of being missed and blaming the design ceiling.
- JSX: wired chamfers={activeSketch.chamfers} and onChamfer={(corner,distance)=>chamferSketchCorner(activeSketch,corner,distance)} into <SketchConstraints/>.

Checks: npx tsc --noEmit clean; npm test exit 0 (full suite, incl. sketch-arc 74 + sketch-outline 67). No test file created; no geometry/data-model file touched.

Hand-trace (no live browser):
(a) Ordinary corner gets a chamfer set: onChamfer(i, v) -> chamferSketchCorner; distance>0, whyCannotChamferCorner returns undefined, writes chamfers[i]=v, onChange fires, outlineOf derives the slice. Cleared at 0: distance not >0, chamfers[i] exists so it deletes the key and onChange fires — corner back to sharp.
(b) Corner whose neighbour already has a CHAMFER, asked to round past the shared edge: roundSketchCorner's fixed lookup finds the neighbour via (f.chamfers?.[c]??0)>0, so the message names that corner ('once corner N has taken its share...') instead of falling into the own-limit branch and blaming the design ceiling.
(c) Reverse — neighbour has a ROUND, asked to chamfer past what's left: chamferSketchCorner's mirrored lookup finds it via (f.rounds?.[c]??0)>0 and the message names the round-holding corner. Both maps checked in both functions.

Parallel/Perpendicular solver extension done. What I changed:

lib/sketch-solve.ts:
- Constraint union: added {kind:'parallel'|'perpendicular', edge, other} (same shape as equal).
- edgeAngle() helper (non-exported, per spec preference -- tests compute angles from returned points via their own atan2).
- rotateEdgeBy() inside solveSketch, next to share(), exactly as spec'd (pinned-aware pivot, arc-length return).
- Constraint-loop branch for parallel/perpendicular, after the length/equal block.
- residualOf() branch converting the angle diff to approximate arc length (units stay distance).
- describe() cases: 'edge N ∥ edge M' / 'edge N ⊥ edge M'.

ONE DEVIATION FROM THE SPEC, and it is load-bearing: the spec's placement note said the length/equal block is continue-terminated so order doesn't matter. It is NOT -- it falls through. As written, a parallel/perpendicular constraint also ran apply(c.edge, target) and stretched its edge to the average of the two lengths, silently destroying the very length rotateEdgeBy exists to preserve. My test item 3 caught it (edge 0 went 40.000 -> 40.447). I guarded the length/equal block to 'if (c.kind==='length'||c.kind==='equal')' with a comment explaining why. After that, length preservation passes both unpinned and pinned. This is a real spec bug, not a style choice -- flagging it for your review.

scripts/sketch-solve-assertions.cjs: added the parallel/perpendicular section covering all 7 spec items (parallel, perpendicular, length-preservation unpinned, length-preservation with one corner pinned + pin-never-moves exact, zero-length refused not NaN'd, the impossible-triangle convergence case, and equal+parallel+perpendicular coexistence). 34 assertions total, all PASS.

TEST ITEM 6 -- THE ONE THAT NEEDS A HUMAN READ: the impossible triangle (3 edges, all three pairs perpendicular) does NOT converge. It runs the full 300 iterations. I traced it: moved is stuck at a constant 15.24 from iteration 50 onward, residual frozen at 35.32, final points finite but the solver never settles. It correctly reports overConstrained=true and never NaNs, but it pinballs at the cap rather than settling on a compromise. Per the spec I did NOT try to fix this -- it is the flagged open question and I'm reporting it as a real algorithmic finding, not papering over it. My test surfaces the iteration count as a MEASURE line (not a hard PASS/FAIL) so the suite stays green while the number is visible for a human.

Checks: npm test FULL EXIT 0 (sketch-solve 34 assertions among them). tsc --noEmit on lib/sketch-solve.ts alone: exit 0. Full-repo tsc --noEmit: exit 2, but ALL THREE errors are in components/SandboxWorkspace.tsx (newPolygonSketch/newRectangleSketch/rollbackIndex) -- pre-existing uncommitted work in that file, unrelated to my change; I confirmed by stashing my edits and re-running (still fails) and by compiling my file in isolation (clean). I did not touch SandboxWorkspace.tsx (out of scope).

NOT done: nothing in scope is unfinished. Out-of-scope untouched: components/ (all), .gauntlet/parity-sketch.json. I could not do a live-browser check (no browser). Releasing my claims on lib/sketch-solve.ts and scripts/sketch-solve-assertions.cjs now.

Parallel/Perpendicular solver extension SIGNED OFF, no rework needed. Your caught bug was real and the fix is correct -- confirmed by reading the diff directly: the length/equal block is now its own if-block ending in continue, and parallel/perpendicular is a separate if-block also ending in continue, so there's no fall-through path left. Good catch, and good instinct to trust your own test over my spec's claim. Independently re-verified everything myself: node scripts/test-sketch-solve.mjs -> ALL PASS (34), including the MEASURE line surfacing the impossible-triangle result exactly as asked (300/300 iterations, not silently hidden behind a bare PASS). Isolated npx tsc --noEmit (stashed every other in-flight file, tested just your two) -> exit 0, confirming the 3 full-repo tsc errors are 100% pre-existing SandboxWorkspace.tsx issues, unrelated to this task. Full npm test in that same isolated state -> exit 0. On the convergence finding: accepting it as a documented, bounded limitation rather than requiring a fix -- it never crashes, never produces NaN, correctly reports overConstrained=true so the existing 'these rules disagree' UI message will fire, and only triggers on a genuinely-impossible 3-way conflict a student would have to deliberately construct. Burning the full 300-iteration budget on that path is a performance non-issue at this sketch size. This is exactly the outcome the design pass's open question was hoping to get -- a real, honest measurement instead of an assumed 'probably fine.' Geometry/solver layer is done. Next: the Rules-panel UI (the N-choose-2 toggle grid for Equal/Parallel/Perpendicular) -- I'll scope that as its own spec.
